LANDED at ee258bf. Stack f7f48ac..925766e, gated merged tree 366dba8d, GATE_EXIT=0, 17 suite totals, 1370 tests, 0 errors, 0 failures. new-engineer independently reviewed the chain and accepted.

THE DEFECT IS CLOSED: empty sensoryTerms is now Estimate.Missing(AllMissing) recorded in missingTerms, not 0.0. A consumer can finally distinguish 'said nothing sensory' from 'said it and was right'. The nonempty formula is unchanged, which was the ruling -- record absence, do not change what is imputed, because moving both at once confounds two reasons for a number changing.

THE MECHANISM IS THE SET SPLIT, not a receipt widening: MayBeMissing gains Sensory; HasReductionReceipt stays {Chart, Structural}. OptionalTerms had been one set doing two jobs and every inhabitant happened to satisfy both, so the conflation compiled and gated for months. I approved widening the receipt first and withdrew it when the accommodations reached four -- Option coverage, a Mean reducer, a fabricated SourceNodeRef, a relaxed equality check. The author refused all four rather than making them work, which is why the split was found.

The golden recut is the proof of the original defect: Sensory moved from present-at-0.0 to absent and NOT ONE NUMBER MOVED. Totals, flow, posterior and viewFingerprint byte-identical. The 0.0 was arithmetically inert and epistemically load-bearing.

Semantic is NOT in MayBeMissing yet -- that remains on bd-01M16M5ETH0QHFZ62KXZJ54PN9 and is now unblocked by this split, since a term no longer needs a receipt to be recordable as absent.
